title: satisfactory values
description: Strict values schema (issue #68). additionalProperties is false on every chart-owned object level, so a key that the chart does not read is rejected at render time instead of being silently ignored. The only objects that stay open are the ones passed verbatim into the Kubernetes pod spec (probes, security contexts, global) - the chart does not interpret their contents, so it cannot judge which keys are meaningful. The hardening, probe and resources blocks additionally accept null, because an erased block falls back to the chart defaults (issue #99). Note that this chart keeps env, probes and securityContext at the TOP level rather than under a chart-named key.

global.description: Helm's conventional cross-chart values. Unused by this chart, kept open so an umbrella install cannot break on it.

debug.description: Passed to the image as DEBUG.

game.description: May be null / empty: the chart then falls back to its documented game defaults (issue #99) instead of aborting the render with a nil-pointer error, which is what an erased block used to do.

experimental.description: Passed to the image as STEAMBETA - switches to the experimental game branch.

enableSeasonalEvents.description: Seasonal (holiday) events. NEGATED by the chart into the image's DISABLESEASONALEVENTS: true renders DISABLESEASONALEVENTS="false" and the events run, false renders "true" and they do not. Only true/false are accepted (boolean or string); anything else aborts the render. Default false, which reproduces what the chart has always rendered - up to 6.1.0 the key was game.seasonalEvents and was passed through unchanged, so its default true wrote DISABLESEASONALEVENTS=true and the events were off despite this description claiming the opposite (issue #215). The old key game.seasonalEvents no longer exists and is rejected here rather than silently ignored.

storage.description: Size of the data PVC. Not null-safe on purpose: an erased value yields an invalid PVC rather than a silently degraded workload.

resources.description: May be null / empty: the chart then falls back to its default requests and computed limits (issue #99) instead of rendering a container without resource accounting. The default limitFactor is 2 here, not the repo-wide 3, to keep the memory limit at the previously published 8Gi.

securityContext.description: May be null / empty at any level: the chart then falls back to its hardening defaults (issue #99) instead of rendering an unhardened workload.

pod.description: Merged onto the chart's pod hardening defaults and rendered as the pod's securityContext; kept open because the chart does not interpret the individual fields.

container.description: Merged onto the chart's container hardening defaults and rendered as the container's securityContext; kept open because the chart does not interpret the individual fields.

probe.description: Merged onto the chart's probe defaults and rendered as a container probe; kept open because the chart does not interpret the individual fields. May be null / empty, which means the defaults apply (issue #99) rather than the probe disappearing.
